title: An Integrated Platform for Studying Learning with Intelligent Tutoring Systems: CTAT+TutorShop
extended_summary:
This paper describes CTAT+TutorShop, an integrated platform for authoring, deploying, and studying intelligent tutoring systems (ITSs). The authors argue that ITSs are not only effective learning technologies, but also valuable research platforms for investigating how students learn, how tutoring systems should be improved, and what learning sciences principles matter in highly scaffolded digital environments.

The paper presents the platform’s capabilities across the full research lifecycle: mining log data to identify learner difficulties, redesigning tutors and problem-selection policies based on those data, and running experimental studies to test alternative ITS features. It emphasizes built-in DataShop-compatible logging, authoring tools for both example-tracing and model-tracing tutors, support for pre/post tests, custom task selection, and experimental condition management through TutorShop.

The paper also summarizes five case studies using CTAT+TutorShop across multiple contexts and domains, including chemistry, mathematics, algebra, and educational games. These examples involve K-12 and higher education learners in classroom and real-world educational settings, and they illustrate comparisons such as polite versus direct feedback, ITS versus paper-based practice, gamified versus standard tutors, and data-driven redesign of an algebra tutor.

Overall, the authors conclude that CTAT+TutorShop has enabled a large body of ITS research and is especially useful because it combines authoring, deployment, logging, and experimentation in one ecosystem. They suggest that the platform supports both basic learning-sciences questions and practical learning-engineering workflows, while also identifying future opportunities to improve study metadata, experimental support, and adaptive testing within the platform.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed platform/case-study paper with extensive references to prior experiments, but it is not itself a controlled evaluation of a single intervention. It is primarily descriptive and synthesis-oriented, so it supports only low-to-moderate evidentiary confidence for causal claims.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper suggests broad, potentially important impact because the platform underpins many tutoring studies and reports positive learning effects in several cited works. However, this article itself does not estimate a single effect size or demonstrate impact directly, so the impact level is best treated as modest/unclear.

interventions.use_case: Platform and case studies on CTAT+Tutorshop for authoring, deploying, and studying rule/model-based intelligent tutoring systems with step-level hints, feedback, mastery learning, and experimental variations in science, math, and related domains.

finding.finding_summary: Across the paper’s cited intervention studies, CTAT-based math tutors generally produced positive learning outcomes, but the paper is mainly a platform/case-study report rather than a single causal estimate. The strongest concrete result described is Huang et al. (2021), where a redesigned Mathtutor led to significantly better learning gains, reduced over- and under-practice, and steeper learning curves in high school Algebra 1 classes (one-month classroom experiment).
finding.measure: Learning gains on pre/post tests; learning curves; over- and under-practice indicators; problem-solving performance

finding.finding_summary: The paper summarizes multiple studies showing that some ITS/game variants improved engagement, while others harmed it. For example, the gamified algebra tutor is described as achieving greater student learning and engagement, whereas another gamification intervention (star system/redo mechanics in Lynnette) was detrimental for learning; thus the engagement-related evidence is mixed across CTAT studies.
finding.measure: Engagement and enjoyment observations/reports; in-study behavioral engagement indicators
finding.study_size: over 1,500 students across Decimal Point studies; other studies not_reported

finding.finding_summary: The platform is described as supporting chemistry and genetics tutoring, including Stoich Tutor and other science-related ITSs, with cited studies reporting effective learning with CTAT-authored tutors. However, this paper does not provide a single pooled effect size for science outcomes; it mainly documents the research infrastructure and references prior science-tutoring studies.
finding.measure: Science problem-solving learning gains in chemistry tutoring contexts

finding.finding_summary: Several cited CTAT studies targeted self-explanation, self-regulated learning, and strategy use, and the paper characterizes these interventions as effective or promising. For example, open learner model and self-regulated learning support studies are presented as improving learning outcomes and supporting learner agency, but the paper does not report a pooled quantitative estimate.
finding.measure: Self-regulated learning behaviors, strategy use, self-assessment, and related learning-process measures
